solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: see 9ac.
Balls covering behind when high?

indicators.note: one thing covering another wraps around it, so the outer letters go either side

parts.note: Ed Balls, the Labour politician, gives his first name
behind schedule is late

explanation.surface: A rude image of testicles covering a backside in a moment of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls is not anatomy but Ed Balls, then Labour's shadow chancellor; his first name wraps around LATE to give ELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being elated means feeling joyful and exhilarated, and high is a common informal synonym for that mood.

clue.text: Gestures very good to crack crimes

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very

indicators.note: cracking something means breaking into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sins are wrongdoings, moral crimes
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Rude hand signs are the sort of thing that helps solve crimes, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside SINS to make SIGNS, after V. A V-sign is the British rude gesture made with two fingers, palm inward.
explanation.definitionFit: V-signs are hand signals, either of victory or, palm inward, a rude insult in Britain.

clue.text: Balls' complete absence of vision, say?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., having none of a sense such as sight

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: vision is one example of a sense, and lacking it entirely would be a non-sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is British slang for rubbish or foolish talk, which is exactly what nonsense means.

clue.text: Doctors know dick can produce a change of gear

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A dig at medics who supposedly know nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Know dick' is slang for knowing nothing, but its eight letters are the material for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Kickdown is when an automatic gearbox drops to a lower ratio as the accelerator is floored, a sudden shift of gear.

clue.text: Takes the line of least resistance — which is pants

definitions.text: Takes the line of least resistance
definitions.meaning: first meaning: an electrical current that short-circuits follows the easiest path

explanation.surface: Someone who always takes the easy way out is judged rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is British slang for rubbish, so the surface reads as a verdict on lazy people; really it means trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity shorts when it bypasses the circuit through the lowest resistance, and shorts are also cut-off trousers.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) Box bed seat conversion, which electioneering Cameron is wary of

definitions.text: which electioneering Cameron is wary of

parts.note: the box is slang for the TV set

indicators.note: a conversion changes something into a different form, so the letters are remade

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Converting a box bed into a seat, something the campaigning Prime Minister avoids.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron, then Prime Minister, was reluctant to take part in televised leaders' debates before the 2015 election.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron resisted head-to-head broadcast clashes with rival party leaders, so these are what he was nervous about while campaigning.

clue.text: Live broadcast with Miliband ("Mad Hatter"), a devious menace?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something mad is deranged, so the word after it is rearranged

parts.note: Ed Miliband was then leader of the Labour Party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A live television appearance by Ed Miliband, cast as the Mad Hatter, looks menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A veiled threat is an indirect, thinly disguised warning of harm, hence a sly or underhand menace.

clue.text: (& 1dn.) Pissed on flag, approaching the top level

parts.note: pissed means drunk, and drunk is high
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: A drunk urinates on a flag as the top brass approach.
explanation.definitionFit: A high standard is the best grade of quality, the uppermost tier anyone might aim for.

clue.text: Blair familiarly crushing fancy rosettes as an alpha male sort of thing

definitions.text: an alpha male sort of thing

indicators.note: crushing something means squeezing it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a familiar shortening of Tony Blair's first name

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tony Blair stamping on prize rosettes like a dominant male.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair's matey nickname is used split in two, with the rearranged letters squeezed between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Testosterone is the male sex hormone associated with dominance and aggression, the stuff macho behaviour is blamed on.

clue.text: (& 26ac.) After big knock — being rejected — 'hot' Nigel staggers on feet, completely finished

parts.note: a rejection is a no, and N is the usual shorthand for no on a voting form

indicators.note: someone who staggers lurches about unsteadily, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written
FT is the abbreviation for feet

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage, rejected by voters, reels about punch-drunk after a heavy blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: the anagram needs one more N than the hot Nigel letters supply, best taken as the no of rejection. Nigel is Nigel Farage, then leader of UKIP.
explanation.definitionFit: When there is nothing left, all is used up or spent, so someone or something is utterly exhausted.

clue.text: Mouthpiece, second to come before Brenda

indicators.note: coming before means placed in front, so the earlier pieces lead

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a crude sense: to climax is to peak
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth, whose royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: A spokesperson who gets in a second before the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called the Queen 'Brenda', so she stands for ER, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker is a spokesperson who talks on behalf of others, and so serves as their mouthpiece.

clue.text: Become rotten piss-covered academic

indicators.note: something covered has a layer wrapped around it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: piss is British slang for weak beer, and ale is beer
a Doctor of Divinity, an academic title abbreviated DD

explanation.surface: A drunken don soaked in urine has gone to the bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that addle go bad, so the verb means to spoil or putrefy.

clue.text: "Bad actions by Poles" which Putin intends to tough out

definitions.text: which Putin intends to tough out

indicators.note: bad here means faulty or wrong, so the letters are in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
the two magnetic or geographic poles, south and north

explanation.surface: Putin shrugs off criticism of supposed misdeeds by Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like the nationality, but it is S and N, the two poles, added to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Western countries imposed economic penalties on Russia over Ukraine, and Putin vowed to endure them without backing down.

clue.text: see 7ac.
Youth's down: arse cock-up

parts.note: both slang for the backside
a fluff is a blunder or botched attempt

explanation.surface: A young man is depressed after a botched sexual encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: Down looks like gloom, but it is the soft hair on a teenager's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumfluff is British slang for the soft, wispy first facial hair of an adolescent boy.

clue.text: Indecision of America: power bound by feeling

indicators.note: something bound by another is enclosed by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: a sense is a feeling
the United States
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: American uncertainty, its might constrained by emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is a state of anxious uncertainty while a decision or outcome remains pending.

clue.text: Extremely Conservative after European city spirit

indicators.note: coming after means placed behind, so the piece it describes goes second

parts.note: Essen is a city in western Germany

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A staunch Tory follows the spirit of a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence and spirit both name the intrinsic core quality of something, and essence is also a distilled extract.

clue.text: At the end of day, the first woman president, losing head and reserve, screwed up

indicators.note: screwed up means messed about, so what is left is jumbled
losing things means they are taken away, here the head and a second chunk

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
taken as written
the head of the word is its first letter
RES is a short form of reserve

explanation.surface: A first female president loses her leadership and composure at the close of day.
explanation.walkthrough: Head here means the first letter, and reserve is shortened to its usual abbreviation before both are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old poetic word for evening, the time when daylight closes.

clue.text: Not what you'd call Boris, working to abandon the PM, Cinders-like

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: David Cameron was then Prime Minister
a machine that is working is on
cinders are ash, so like them is ashy

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson, scheming to desert Cameron, leaves early like Cinderella.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinders is also Cinderella, who abandons the ball, but here it is just burnt ash.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson loves publicity, so someone who shuns photographers is the opposite of how anyone would describe him.

clue.text: One always chasing talent: "Love wife to be put in nun's place"

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside another piece

parts.note: a nun lives in a cell in her convent
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An adulterer's line: love the wife but lock her in a convent.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Cowell is the music mogul who judges TV talent shows such as The X Factor.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Cowell built his career scouting singers on talent contests, forever pursuing the next star.

clue.text: Brown-noser's affirmative piece

parts.note: the word of agreement
a piece in chess or draughts is a man

explanation.surface: A toady's agreeable piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown hovers in the surface, but brown-noser is just slang for a sycophant.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man always agrees with the boss to curry favour, which is exactly what a sycophantic crawler does.

clue.text: Issue of Eye nearly starts petition

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are taken

parts.note: the initial letters of the two words
to sue is to petition a court

explanation.surface: An edition of Private Eye almost launches a petition.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue looks like a magazine number, but it is a verb meaning to follow on.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a result, which is one sense of the verb to issue.

clue.text: Drink, dear? Here's a means of passing water

parts.note: to sip is to drink
hon, short for honey, is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: Offering a drink to a darling, with a lavatorial afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: Passing water suggests urinating, but a siphon is a tube that moves liquid from one container to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A siphon is a bent tube that draws liquid over a rim and down into a lower vessel.

clue.text: Gnome slips into kinky wear for benefit

indicators.note: slipping into something means going inside it
kinky means twisted, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written
a gnome and an elf are both small folklore creatures

explanation.surface: Lord Gnome, Private Eye's proprietor, slips into fetish gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's fictional owner, so the surface pokes fun at the magazine's own boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare is state support such as social security payments, which Britons commonly call benefit.

clue.text: Throw weight about, being s-sexy lay

parts.note: the stammered first letter
hot is slang for sexy
to lay something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone throwing their weight around while stammering about a sexy partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Lay looks like the sexual noun, but it is the verb meaning to place.
explanation.definitionFit: The shot put is the athletics event in which a heavy metal ball is hurled as far as possible.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Opportunity for a deflection to the left to avoid a catastrophic career?

definitions.text: Opportunity for a deflection to the left to avoid a catastrophic career?

parts.words: Opportunity for a deflection to the left to avoid a catastrophic career?
parts.note: surface reading: a politician swerving leftward to save a doomed political career

parts.words: deflection to the left to avoid a catastrophic career
parts.note: setter's reading: a racing car careering off course veers onto a side lane built for safety

explanation.surface: A politician's chance to lurch leftward and rescue a disastrous career.
explanation.walkthrough: Career is a verb in disguise: to career is to rush out of control, as a car does when its brakes fail.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape road is a side lane off a track or steep road where a runaway vehicle can safely stop.
